author: Vincent of Lérins
translation: C. A. Heurtley (NPNF 2nd series, vol. 11), public domain
note: The 'Vincentian Canon' (c. AD 434) — the test of catholic orthodoxy: the faith held everywhere, always, and by all. 'Catholic' here means UNIVERSAL (the creedal 'one holy catholic Church'), not the Roman communion; the canon is cited approvingly across Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions as the rule for identifying the core faith, which is exactly this site's denominational-neutrality ethos. New author; post-Nicene. Verified verbatim against source_url (apologia-citations, web, 2026-08-24; confirmed 'by all', not the common 'and by all' drift).
text: Moreover, in the Catholic Church itself, all possible care must be taken, that we hold that faith which has been believed everywhere, always, by all.
